phrases-22-47-a-day-with-your-lord-is-li.title: Answering Scoffers: 'A Day With Your Lord Is Like a Thousand Years'
phrases-22-47-a-day-with-your-lord-is-li.note: When challengers demand that punishment be hurried, Surah 22:47 replies that 'God will not break His promise; surely a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count,' matching 2 Peter 3:8–9 and Psalm 90:4 (LXX 89:4).

discussion.view: Exegetes note that this verse answers Meccan sceptics who mocked the delay of divine judgment by contrasting human time with God's eternal measure.
discussion.reply: While Psalm 90:4 (LXX 89:4) introduces the comparison of a thousand years to a day passed, 2 Peter 3:8–9 specifically deploys the maxim ('with the Lord one day is like a thousand years. The Lord is not slow about His promise') to answer scoffers questioning the delay of judgment—the exact rhetorical context and sequence reproduced in Surah 22:47.

phrases-22-47-a-day-with-your-lord-is-li.quranEn: They seek to hurry you with the punishment. God will not break His promise. Surely a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count.
quranHighlights: God will not break His promise. Surely a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count.

sources.title: Second Epistle of Peter (NASB)
sources.en: But do not let this one [fact] escape your notice, beloved, that with the Lord one day is like a thousand years, and a thousand years like one day. The Lord is not slow about His promise, as some count slowness, but is patient toward you, not wishing for any to perish but for all to come to repentance.
highlights: with the Lord one day is like a thousand years, and a thousand years like one day. The Lord is not slow about His promise

sources.title: Psalms (LXX / Septuagint)
sources.en: For a thousand years in your sight are as the yesterday which is past, and as a watch in the night.
highlights: For a thousand years in your sight are as the yesterday which is past
